items.title: SPICE: Sparse Parameter Gossip for LLM Pretraining
items.summary: Pretraining language models across geographically distributed resources requires communication-efficient methods that operate under limited and variable internet bandwidth. Decentralized training replaces global collectives with peer exchanges, but full-model messages make larger peer neighborhoods costly. We introduce SPICE, which combines sparse parameter gossip with error feedback through corrected parameter values that remain directly interpretable as peer neighborhoods change. items.title: Keep the Agent Warm: How ATOM Serves AgentX Workloads on AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs
items.summary: A coding agent makes many model calls in one session, and each one re-sends almost everything before it: one recorded session makes 198 calls, and call #48 sends 195.5K tokens, only 1.3K of them new. Agentic workloads combine long shared histories and short outputs, interrupted by tool calls and parallel sub-agents. Serving them well takes more than raw GPU compute: it means keeping the agent warm, with its history cached and its decode moving when new requests arrive.

items.summary: GEMM and attention kernels already have offline tuning paths. The kernels around them often do not. A compiled inference graph still launches a long tail of small Triton kernels for casts, concatenations, normalizations, activations, gathers, and histogram-style updates. items.title: TAILROLL: Tail-Aware Rollout Acceleration for RL-Based LLM Post-Training
items.summary: RL post-training of large language models (LLMs) is bottlenecked by rollout: heavy-tailed responses leave engines idle as each step waits for the longest response. Asynchronous training masks, but does not eliminate, idle time. We distinguish imbalance waste (uneven placement and decode contention) from straggler waste (waiting for the longest response).
